database_summary: Small e-commerce / web-analytics style schema with user master(s), many event/log tables (actions, activity, reads, forms), product master snapshots (dated tables), category master, purchase and sales aggregates. Logs are mostly event-level (append-only) with timestamp strings. Some tables are duplicates/variants (with_ip, with_noise, invalid, dup). No declared foreign keys in DDL. Several small lookup/master tables hold descriptive attributes.

accepted.name: events_action_log_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.session AS session,
  a.user_id AS user_id,
  a.action AS action,
  a.category AS category,
  a.products AS products,
  a.amount AS amount,
  a.stamp AS stamp,
  u.sex AS sex,
  u.birth_date AS birth_date,
  u.register_date AS register_date,
  u.register_device AS register_device,
  u.withdraw_date AS withdraw_date
FROM action_log a
LEFT JOIN mst_users u
  ON a.user_id = u.user_id
accepted.description: Event-level action_log joined to mst_users to expose user attributes alongside each action. Useful for analyses that need user demographics (sex, register_date, register_device) with each action event. | Use for: Segment actions by user demographic (e.g., actions by sex or register_device); Compute per-user or per-demographic aggregates of amount or event counts; Join to product or category masters after splitting products

accepted.name: users_active_master
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  user_id AS user_id,
  sex AS sex,
  birth_date AS birth_date,
  register_date AS register_date,
  register_device AS register_device,
  withdraw_date AS withdraw_date
FROM mst_users
WHERE withdraw_date IS NULL
accepted.description: Subset of mst_users representing active users (not withdrawn). Use for cohorts restricted to currently active users. | Use for: Cohort analyses limited to active users; Retention and engagement metrics for users who haven't withdrawn

accepted.name: purchase_agg_per_user
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  user_id AS user_id,
  COUNT(purchase_id) AS purchase_count,
  SUM(amount) AS total_amount,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(purchase_id) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE AVG(amount) END AS average_amount,
  MAX(stamp) AS last_purchase_stamp
FROM purchase_log
GROUP BY user_id
accepted.description: Aggregated purchase metrics per user: total purchases, total amount, average amount, last purchase timestamp. Useful for LTV, RFM, and user-level purchase summaries. | Use for: Compute user LTV or segmentation (RFM); Join purchase summaries to user demographics or event behavior

accepted.name: product_sales_ranked
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id AS product_id,
  category_name AS category_name,
  sales AS sales,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category_name ORDER BY sales DESC) AS sales_rank
FROM product_sales
accepted.description: Product-level sales with a rank ordered by sales within each category. Exposes rank so downstream queries can filter top-N per category by WHERE rank <= N. | Use for: Top-N products by sales within each category; Compare rank changes when joining to another time snapshot

accepted.name: mst_products_latest_union
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT product_id AS product_id, name AS name, price AS price, updated_at AS updated_at, 'mst_products_20161201' AS source_table
FROM mst_products_20161201
UNION ALL
SELECT product_id AS product_id, name AS name, price AS price, updated_at AS updated_at, 'mst_products_20170101' AS source_table
FROM mst_products_20170101
accepted.description: Union of product master snapshots (mst_products_20161201, mst_products_20170101) with source_stamp to track origin. Useful for analyzing product changes across snapshots and selecting the latest record per product. | Use for: Identify product attribute changes over time; Select the latest product record per product_id using a RANK over updated_at

accepted.name: products_latest_per_product
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id AS product_id,
  name AS name,
  price AS price,
  updated_at AS updated_at
FROM (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    name,
    price,
    updated_at,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY updated_at DESC) AS rn
  FROM (
    SELECT product_id, name, price, updated_at FROM mst_products_20161201
    UNION ALL
    SELECT product_id, name, price, updated_at FROM mst_products_20170101
  )
) WHERE rn = 1
accepted.description: Latest product record per product_id from the unioned product snapshots. Use when you need a single canonical product row (latest updated_at) for joins with events. | Use for: Join events to a single current product master; Report current price or name for product-level revenue calculations

accepted.name: activity_sessions_latest
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  session AS session,
  stamp AS stamp,
  action AS action,
  option AS option,
  path AS path,
  search_type AS search_type
FROM (
  SELECT
    session,
    stamp,
    action,
    option,
    path,
    search_type,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY session ORDER BY stamp DESC) AS rn
  FROM activity_log
)
WHERE rn = 1
accepted.description: Latest activity event per session (most recent stamp). Useful to identify session end time or last action for session-level summarization. | Use for: Sessionization and session-level metrics; Join latest session activity to user_id via action_log or access_log
